- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after spikes.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% to align with historical volatility.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts late-period prices (last 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–3% for final 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +1.3, -0.5, +1.2), model tends to misalign with trend; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to dampen extremes.
